title: Converge trace exporters and introduce low-cpu telemetry fast-paths
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: our runtime currently feeds traces through three different exporter implementations (jaeger/otlp/legacy-json) with per-exporter buffering and format conversion. This increases CPU cost, amplifies tail latency during bursts, and makes sampling rules hard to reason about. Goal: consolidate exporters behind a lightweight shim that normalizes spans once and routes to configured backends, and add a low-CPU fast-path for high-throughput inference processes that avoids full span marshaling for common request shapes. Deliverables: (1) single exporter adapter (shim) with in-memory normalized envelope, (2) incremental opt-in fast-path that emits compact span stubs for common requests and full spans only when sampling/sample-rate triggers, (3) config to enable per-tenant fast-path and fallback, (4) benchmark and rollout plan with canary on dedicated pools.
acceptance_criteria: Single exporter shim replaces duplicate exporter adapters and is feature-equivalent for OTLP export targets
CPU usage reduced: p95 CPU for runtime worker processes decreases by at least 25% in controlled benchmarks for typical token-generation workloads
Span cardinality does not increase; tag enrichment preserved for audited tenants
No increased error-rate in trace export path (error budget + alerts unchanged) after canary rollout
Config gating exists and is documented; ability to disable fast-path per-tenant without restart
Automated tests covering normalization logic and fallback when exporter fails
comments: 2025-02-12 - Triage: flagged as P1 techno-debt for next infra sprint. Assigned to Julian. Initial notes collected and opened design doc.

2025-02-14 - Design sync: decided to implement normalization at the runtime ingress to avoid duplicate conversions deeper in the stack. Trade-off: adds a small allocation on warm path but eliminates repeated marshal/unmarshal cycles.

2025-02-20 - Benchmarking: prototype fast-path that writes a compact span stub (name + duration + sampled=false bit) shows ~28% CPU reduction in local microbenchmarks for batch size 16 workloads. Link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/bench/telemetry-fastpath
2025-02-25 - PR opened for exporter shim core: github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/1382. Basic shim + tests included. Requesting design review from @marco and @sophia.

2025-03-01 - Review feedback: addressed threading model concerns (use single-producer ringbuf + background batcher), added metrics for dropped spans. Also added integration test to validate OTLP conversion fidelity.

2025-03-04 - Canary plan drafted: rollout to 5% of dedicated pool traffic in two stages with automatic rollback on export error spike > 0.5% or increase in span processing latency > 50ms. Canary playbook saved to Confluence.
Notes: expect follow-up tickets to extend fast-path to embedding workers and to sweep older legacy-json exporters out of repos.
implementation_notes: Prefer zero-copy where possible: reuse proto buffers for OTLP when sampler decides to keep full span
Background batcher will have soft backpressure: drop non-sampled stubs when queue > 32k entries and emit 'dropped_span' metric
Add explicit metric labels: exporter.kind, tenant.id, fastpath.enabled to monitor adoption and regressions
Avoid changing public span schema: normalization maps legacy fields to current attributes but keeps original trace/span ids intact
